A Judgment of volte-face recorded by Appellate Judge in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 20 of 2004 overturning a verdict pronounced by learned Trial Judge in Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2002 under section 96 of The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951 has been challenged by pre-emptor as petitioner on presentation of a Civil Revision petition envisaged under section 115 of The Code. Challenge has been thrown towards first-opposite party who has been characterized as associate of pre-emptees who is no other than father of pre-emptees nineteenth-twenty-first-opposite par-ties. Civil Revision petition has been numbered as Civil Revision Case No. 4077 of 2004. 

 3. Portrayal of essential fact forming backdrop of Civil Revision Case is succinctly stated which is as follows: Petitioner of Civil Revision case as pre-emptor laid a pre-emption Miscellaneous Case under section 96 of The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for an order of pre-emption against purchasers-preemptees who were first-third-opposite parties in pre-emption Miscellaneous Case and Nineteenth-twenty-first opposite parties in this Revision petition in respect of 7 acres of land duly described in schedule to pre-emption Miscellaneous case, Father of pre-emptees had been made First opposite party in Revision Petition depicting him as associate of pre-emptees. Pre-emptor-petitioner exercised his right of pre-emption in the capacity of co-sharer by inheritance. Pre-emptees-opposite parties had been marked as strangers to pre-emption proceeding land. In pre-emption Miscellaneous case it was asserted that no notice of transfer had been served upon him. Pre-emptor-petitioner claimed that Fourth opposite party of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case, father of preemptee opposite parties who was, also, characterized as agent (9419) on 10-1-2002 approached on pre-emption proceeding land to dig earth and on asking by pre-emptor-petitioner, agent Fourth opposite party made disclosure that they purchased pre-emption proceeding land by a deed of conveyance from fifth-tenth opposite parties of pre-emption miscellaneous case.

 20. "Acquiescence" stated in Corpus Juris Secundum (CJS) 1A 279 is as hereunder: 

 The word is further defined as meaning release or abandonment of one's rights if, having rights, he stands by and sees another dealing with his property in a manner inconsistent with such right, and makes no objection while the act is in progress; resting apparently satisfied, without objection; resting satisfied with or submission to an existing state of things; silence and inaction; silent but conscious; silent passive assent; submission; tacit encouragement. In addition, it has generally been said that "acquiescence" is where a person who knows that he is entitled to impeach a transaction or to enforce a right neglects to do so for such a length of time that under the circumstances of the case the other party may fairly infer that he has waived or abandoned his right." 

 "Acquiescence" as stated in Wharton's Law Lexicon Fourteenth Edition is consent, either express or implied. 

 25. Learned Appellate Judge taking into account evidence of OPW 1, OPW 2 and OPW 3 as well as evidence of PW 2 and PW 3 found that pre-emptor-petitioner was approached to purchase land under pre-emption proceeding and pre-emptor-petitioner did not purchase land and right of pre-emptor to pre-empt land stood extinguished. Decision rendered by learned Appellate Judge rested upon proper and correct evaluation and assessment of testimonies of OPW 1, OPW 2, OPW 3 and PW 2 and PW 3. Appellate Judge did not find any ground to disbelieve evidence adduced by witnesses stated above. Learned Trial Judge committed a substantial error in holding that act of mediation on part of pre-emptor in respect of sale matter could not be established. That finding was not based on correct assessment and evaluation of evidence and materials on record. 

 27. Decisions of Court of Appeal being last and final court of fact are not open to interference in Revisional Jurisdiction under section 115 of The Code unless it is show that decisions have been based upon gross misreading of evidence or those have been founded on misconception or misapplication or misapprehension of law or of any misinterpretation of any, material document or otherwise perverse being contrary to law, evidence and materials brought on record. Support for the above proposition is sought to be drawn from a series of decisions, both of our and foreign Jurisdictions. Durga Choudhurain vs Jawahir Singh Choudhuri, 17 Indian Appeal 122, Ramchandra vs Ram Lingam, AIR 1963 SC 302, Abdul Mazid and others vs Khalil Ahmed, PLD 1955 FC 38, Azizur Rahman vs Per Vaizshan and others 1997 PSC 1329, Fazal Karim vs Abdul Manafard and others 1997 PSC 1163, Federal Radid Commission vs Nelson Brothers Board and Mortgage Company and others (1932) vs National Relations Board (1942) 319 US 533, Guejt Heluering, Commissioner of International Revenue vs Johan Kehoe, (1939) 309 US 267, State of New York and others vs United States of America (1946)331 US 284, Fakhruddin Mia and another vs Md Khoda Baksh Sheikh, 29 DLR (SC) 268, Akrab Ali vs Zahiruddin Kari 30 DLR (SC) 81, Abdul Matin Chowdhury vs Chapala Rani Sen and others, 37 DLR (AD) 205, Naimuddin Sardar vs Md Abdul Kalam Biswas 41 DLR (AD) 3, Jasimuddin Kanchan vs Md Ali Ashraf 42 DLR (AD) 289, Mazhurul Borhan vs AH Bhuiyan 1995 BLD (AD) 237 and Haider-un-nessa and another vs Monowara Begum and others 1996 BLD (AD) 280 are some authorities for the aforesaid proposition.
